events.text:
**Recommendation:** Grand Haven is my pick, but I expect all four piers to be slow this week. Nothing in the data shows salmon near any pier right now.

| Port | Pier rating (0–4) |
|---|---|
| Grand Haven | **1** (below average) |
| St. Joseph | **1** |
| South Haven | **0–1** |
| Muskegon | **0–1** |

These ratings are my own expectations, not anything the DNR reported.

**What the reports say**
- **No pier reports this year.** All 2024 salmon reports from June 18 to July 24 are boat reports, so I have no direct pier evidence for this season.
- **Grand Haven (newest report, 2024-07-24, 6 days old):**
  - Boaters caught Chinook, with a few steelhead and coho, 35–100 ft down in 60–120 ft of water. Green and orange spoons and white flasher flies worked (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).
  - Only "a few salmon" came on green meat rigs and glow plugs, rated 1, below average (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).
  - The week before was rated 2, average (Grand Haven, 2024-07-10).
- **Muskegon, South Haven and St. Joseph (latest reports 2024-07-10, 20 days old):**
  - Muskegon was average, with fish 40–100 ft down in 70–120 ft of water (Muskegon, 2024-07-10).
  - South Haven was average, with fish in 75–110 ft of water on rotators and flies (South Haven, 2024-07-10).
  - St. Joseph was excellent (4), with spoons in 80–90 ft of water (St. Joseph, 2024-07-10). That was a boat bite offshore, and the report is three weeks old.
- **Water now (measured by buoys, last week's average):** St. Joseph 73 F, South Haven 71 F, Grand Haven and Muskegon 68 F. Each is up only about 1–2 F over the week, so there is no sharp drop that would signal an upwelling.
- **Not available:** The conditions tool returned buoy summaries only. I have no pierhead temperatures, modeled cold-layer depths or wind forecast for this week.

**History (same time of year, earlier seasons)**
- Pier salmon fishing is usually thin in late July and early August.
- Grand Haven pier anglers caught "a few salmon on glow plugs," rated 1 (Grand Haven, 2023-08-02).
- St. Joseph piers were "a little on the slow side," with a few coho on nightcrawlers and steelhead on shrimp (St. Joseph, 2023-08-09). That was right after an upwelling, and it was still slow.
- Boat fishing in those weeks was decent to good, with fish well offshore at 50–140 ft down in 80–160 ft of water.

**My read**
- General guidance from Michigan Sea Grant/MSU Extension says north or east winds push warm surface water offshore and cold water up along the shore. That upwelling is what brings salmon toward pierheads.
- The lake is warm and stratified, and the buoys show no cold-water event. I'd expect most salmon to be offshore in 60–120 ft of water, well beyond pier range.
- I'd put Grand Haven first because it has the most recent report, a pier catch of salmon on glow plugs in a past season, and the coolest water (68 F). Expect a few fish at best.
- St. Joseph's offshore bite was the strongest in July, but its water is the warmest (73 F) and pier results there were poor in the past.
- South Haven and Muskegon have no pier evidence and older reports, so I rate them lowest.
- If you go, fish glow plugs or glow spoons at dawn or dusk. Those were the lures and the low-light conditions mentioned for Grand Haven.
- If a north or east wind blows for a day or two, check the pierhead water temperature. A sharp drop there would be worth rating higher, and it would favor whichever pier cools most.

**Caveats:** The reports are 6–20 days old, and none of them cover piers in 2024.
